title: Lighthouse: On Building a Trustworthy Digital Assistant for Exploring History with Civil Rights Archives
abstract: arXiv:2610.30158v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), as a decision-support aid, provides new tools for studying history effectively using multimodal data, including text, images, and audio. We present, to our knowledge, the first digital assistant named Lighthouse--commonly called a chatbot--for exploring the Civil Rights period of the United States using data from South Carolina. From an AI perspective, the system's novelty lies in its guiding design principles of (a) focusing on trustworthiness of content and (b) by modeling and reducing potential harm to users from generated answers. It implements these with a neuro-symbolic approach that combines neural learning through a large language model (LLM) with rule-based symbolic solving, balancing risk of answers with generality of coverage. translated_title: Lighthouse：构建一个基于民权档案探索历史的可信赖数字助手
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）作为一种决策辅助工具，为利用包括文本、图像和音频在内的多模态数据高效研究历史提供了新的工具。据我们所知，我们提出了第一个名为Lighthouse的数字助手（通常称为聊天机器人），用于基于南卡罗来纳州的数据探索美国民权时期的历史。从AI的角度来看，该系统的新颖之处在于其指导性设计原则： 关注内容的可信性； 通过对生成的答案可能对用户造成的潜在伤害进行建模并加以减少。系统通过一种神经符号方法来实现这些原则，该方法将大型语言模型（LLM）的神经学习与基于规则的符号求解相结合，在答案的风险与覆盖面的广泛性之间取得平衡。我们使用具有单一可接受答案的事实性客观问题以及主观问题对Lighthouse进行评估。对于后者，一个主观数据集……
tldr: 该论文提出了首个用于探索美国民权时期历史的可信赖数字助手Lighthouse，其创新在于采用神经符号方法（结合大语言模型与基于规则的符号求解），以内容可信度和减少生成答案的潜在伤害为核心设计原则。
en_tdlr: This paper presents Lighthouse, the first trustworthy digital assistant for exploring U.S. Civil Rights history, whose novelty lies in a neuro-symbolic approach combining an LLM with rule-based symbolic reasoning, guided by design principles of content trustworthiness and minimizing potential harm from generated answers.
